misconceptions.e-not-squared: Used e for the height ratio. e is a speed ratio; height goes with speed squared.
misconceptions.finite-bounces: Thought the model ball stops after a few bounces.
misconceptions.first-drop-twice: Counted the first drop as if it went up and down.
misconceptions.ignores-shrink: Forgot that each bounce is lower than the last.
misconceptions.infinite-sum-infinite: Thought infinitely many bounces must add up to an infinite distance.
misconceptions.kept-vs-lost: Used the fraction lost instead of the fraction kept.
misconceptions.loss-fraction: Used 1 − e, the fraction of speed lost.
misconceptions.off-by-one: Counted one bounce too few or too many.
misconceptions.one-way-only: Counted only the fall (or only the rise) of each bounce.
misconceptions.skipped-a-bounce: Applied the fraction twice for one bounce.

outcome: Each bounce keeps the same fraction of the height, a geometric sequence, and infinitely many bounces cover a finite distance.
